title.narrative: ADB Clean Energy Financing Partnership Facility
ADB Clean Energy Financing Partnership Facility

description.narrative: CEFs huvudsakliga mål är att finansiera projekt inom "ren Energi", dvs. förnybart, energieff, och tillgång till energi. Fonden finansierar även pilotprojekt, utveckling av policy, finansieringsmetoder etc. för att stimulere ren energi.

Clean Energy Fund is part of ADB Clean Energy Financing Partnership Facility. Main objective to finance projects in clean energy, major demonstration projects, policy development and mode of fundings.

The Clean Energy Financing Partnership Facility (CEFPF) was established in 2007 to help improve energy security in Developing Member Countries (DMCs) and decrease the rate of climate change. It will do this by financing the deployment of new, more efficient and less polluting supply and end-use technologies, through either grant or non-grant resources. The CEFPF is composed of the Clean Energy Fund (CEF), the Asian Clean Energy Fund (ACEF), the Carbon Capture and Storage Fund (CCSF) and the Canadian Climate Fund for the Private Sector in Asia (CFPS).

sector.narrative: Energy generation, renewable sources - multiple technologies

description.narrative:
The CEFPF has made substantial advancements in several key areas in 2023:
Investment Mobilization: CEFPF has successfully mobilized substantial clean energy investments, reaching $6.1 billion in cumulative ADB leveraged investments, well on track to meet or exceed targets.
Deployment of New Technologies: Out of 60 targeted new technologies, 52 have been implemented, reflecting significant progress, though challenges remain, particularly with less tested technologies.
Energy Access: The facility has provided energy access to 393,985 households, with a goal of reaching 700,000, but additional focus will be needed to achieve this goal.
Gender Mainstreaming and Benefits: CEFPF has made progress in promoting gender inclusion, with 82% of access-to-energy projects including gender components, approaching the 90% target.
Policy and Financial Models: CEFPF has supported the development of 22 enabling policies and 21 financial models, slightly below the 2025 goals but continuing to make steady progress.
In terms of progress toward outcome:
Renewable Energy: In 2023, the target for installed renewable energy capacity was achieved. Notably, the technical assistance (TA) for Indias Assam Solar Project is expected to contribute significantly, supporting the installation of a 500 MW and a 250 MW solar PV facility in Assams Karbi Anglong district. To date, CEFPF-supported projects are expected to install 3,672 MW of renewable energy capacity and generate 8.7 TWh of renewable energy annually.
Gender Equality Promotion: The CEFPF continues to advance gender equality in the energy sector, supporting ADBs Strategy 2030 goal to have at least 75% of ADBs committed operations promoting gender equality by 2030. In 2023, CEFPF is backing ten projects that promote gender equality, with three classified as Effective Gender Mainstreaming (EGM). These include the regional TA for Promoting Energy Transition through Regional Cooperation and Integration in South Asia, the TA for Indias Assam Solar Project, and the TA for Indias Madhya Pradesh Renewable Energy Project.
Policy Development Support: To date, the CEFPF has supported the creation of 22 policies aimed at enabling clean energy development or advancing Carbon Capture, Utilization, and Storage (CCUS).
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
